justification: The verify app showed SEPP/LEP instruments as verified/current even after legislation_monitor.py detected an amendment: needs_review (set on instrument_registry) was never surfaced — the currency API read only instrument_currency, so the UI judged currency by verified_at age alone. A freshly 'verified' instrument that was since amended still showed green. This makes 'verified' fail closed: the API now joins needs_review, and InstrumentCurrency flips that instrument (and the overall dot) to amber 'change found at source — under review', suppressing the stale verified date/version, until a human reconciles.

pre_impl.existing_data: needs_review already exists on instrument_registry (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, idx_ir_review), set TRUE by legislation_monitor.py on a detected amendment and cleared by update_instrument_provisions.py after human reconcile. instrument_currency has no such column; the API queried only instrument_currency so the flag never reached the UI.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The currency UI assumed verified_at freshness captured currency. It does not: an instrument can be recently verified yet already amended (needs_review TRUE). Age does not encode a detected-but-unreconciled change, so green could be shown on a superseded instrument.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new table or endpoint. The existing instrument_currency SELECT gains a LEFT JOIN to instrument_registry to read needs_review (COALESCE FALSE). The component adds a statusFor() override reusing the existing statusDot/daysSince; no new fetch.

functions.name: GET
functions.input: the council slug taken from the request query string
functions.output: currency rows for that council plus NULL-council state instruments, each now carrying needs_review (COALESCE r.needs_review FALSE)
functions.if_none: missing council -> 400; a currency row with no matching instrument_registry row (e.g. DCP) -> needs_review FALSE via COALESCE

functions.name: statusFor
functions.input: a single instrument currency row returned by the API
functions.output: {color,title,underReview}: amber under-review override when needs_review, else the freshness dot from statusDot(daysSince(verified_at))
functions.if_none: needs_review false/absent -> falls through to the existing freshness logic; null verified_at -> statusDot returns the grey 'not yet verified' state

values: N/A - no regulatory values. needs_review is a monitor-set flag read from instrument_registry; the component never invents it.
queries: N/A for new queries - extends the existing instrument_currency SELECT with a LEFT JOIN instrument_registry ON r.instrument_key = ic.instrument_key, same WHERE (ic.council = $1 OR ic.council IS NULL); no new table or endpoint.

break_it.scenario: needs_review is NULL for a currency row with no instrument_registry row (DCP rows)
break_it.what_happens: an unguarded NULL could render as under-review (false alarm) or break the boolean check
break_it.repro: load a council whose DCP instrument_currency rows have no registry match
break_it.how: COALESCE(r.needs_review, FALSE) in SQL guarantees a boolean; the TS type is boolean and statusFor treats only TRUE as under-review, so DCP rows render normally

break_it.scenario: An instrument is amended (needs_review TRUE) but the panel still shows green/verified — the exact bug being fixed
break_it.what_happens: a superseded citation would be presented as current
break_it.repro: set instrument_registry.needs_review = TRUE for sepp_housing_2021 and open a property
break_it.how: statusFor checks needs_review FIRST and overrides colour+title; the overall dot uses anyReview; the stale version_label and verified date are suppressed and replaced with the under-review note

break_it.scenario: The LEFT JOIN multiplies rows if instrument_registry had more than one row per instrument_key
break_it.repro: two registry rows sharing an instrument_key
break_it.how: instrument_key is unique on instrument_registry (and instrument_currency is unique on (council, instrument_key)), so the join is 1:1; no fan-out

post_merge.db_reset: N/A - no schema or data change; needs_review column already exists.
post_merge.secrets: None - no new secrets or env vars.
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the Next.js frontend auto-deploys on Vercel from GitHub on merge; backend/API unchanged.
post_merge.manual_verify: Set instrument_registry.needs_review = TRUE for a state instrument (e.g. sepp_housing_2021); open a property in any council -> the Data currency dot and that instrument's row show amber 'change found at source — under review' with the verified date/version suppressed. Set it back to FALSE -> the verified date returns. Confirm DCP rows (no registry row) still render their verified date normally.
